title: end-to-end-change-control-for-model-rollouts-with-dynamic-signoffs
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Define and deliver an end-to-end change control system for model production rollouts that combines RBAC-driven approvals, audit logging, evidence bundles, dynamic signoff requirements based on risk, and integrated rollback policies for canaries, A/B tests, and shadow traffic. This ticket scopes the product & UX requirements, acceptance criteria, and handoff to ENG for implementation of console workflows and API primitives.

Context: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private deployments, customers require stricter, auditable controls for model changes. Existing lightweight canary and A/B tooling lacks structured signoff flows, RBAC bindings for approvers, and standardized evidence capture for audits. We must support both automated CI-driven deployments (via API) and manual console-driven rollouts while ensuring a consistent change control audit trail and automatic safety rollbacks when thresholds are breached.

Goals:
- Define RBAC roles/permission surface for rollout actions (submit, approve, veto, audit-view).
- Design approval flows that can be static (fixed approvers) or dynamic (chain of signoffs determined by risk rules).
- Capture and store an evidence bundle per rollout (prompts/seed inputs, evaluation results, dashboards, PR links).
- Surface and enforce timeboxed signoffs and escalation rules.
- Integrate with existing audit logs and export format for compliance teams.
- Define auto-rollback triggers (latency, error-rate, quality-regression) and safe fallback models.
- API-first design so platform automation & CI systems can orchestrate signoffs and rollbacks.

Scope (in): Approval UX + API, RBAC definitions & enforcement, evidence bundle schema, audit-log integration, rollout policy editor (rules for dynamic signoffs), auto-rollback triggers & policy linkage, telemetry metrics to evaluate rollouts.

Scope (out): Full SSO/SCIM integration (handled by separate security ticket), on-prem storage variant of evidence bundles (investigate later), training/regulatory paperwork for customers.
tasks: Product: finalize signoff role taxonomy and permission matrix
Design: screens for create rollout -> attach signoffs -> evidence bundle preview -> approval modal
Eng: API endpoints for create-rollout, submit-evidence, request-approval, set-approval-rule, trigger-rollback
Eng: backend: link rollout records to existing audit-log stream and long-term retention store
Eng: implement dynamic signoff engine (evaluate risk rules, expand approver set, timebox enforcement)
Eng: auto-rollback controller with configurable signal detectors (99p latency, 5xx rate, quality delta from eval metrics)
QA: integration tests with canary traffic simulation, shadow traffic diffing, A/B metric guardrails
Docs: public API docs and admin runbook for on-call and SRE
acceptance_criteria: Console: admin can create a rollout with at least one approval stage and assign approvers or choose dynamic rules
API: CI can create rollout and attach a JSON evidence bundle; response includes rollback policy ID
RBAC: roles (rollout_submitter, rollout_approver, rollout_vetoer, audit_viewer) enforced across UI and API
Audit: every state transition (submit/request-approval/approve/reject/rollback) is emitted to audit logs with user ID and evidence bundle reference
Dynamic signoff: risk rules can require additional approvers if model size > threshold OR customer_impact=high
Auto-rollback: system triggers rollback and marks rollout as failed when any configured detector crosses threshold and rollback completed within defined SLO
Evidence bundle: stores links to PRs, eval run IDs, screenshots of slices, baseline vs new-model metric diffs
A/B & Shadow: traffic configs respect approval gates (shadow deployments can be started without approval for internal experiments but must be gated for customer-impacting changes)
decisions: Use a hybrid model: console-first UX plus API primitives to enable automation; do not build separate approval backends.
Evidence bundles will be stored as metadata references (ids/uris) rather than large binary payloads to keep audit log size manageable.
Dynamic signoff engine uses a simple rule DSL (key, operator, value) evaluated at rollout creation time; complex policy composition deferred.
Auto-rollback signals are initially limited to latency (p99), error-rate (5xx/%), and quality delta from eval harness; SLA-based signals to come later.
risks: Over-complex approval flows may slow down iteration for PLG users — mitigate by offering 'fast-path' for non-customer-impacting rollouts.
Evidence bundle metadata retention could contain PII or sensitive prompts; require redaction policies and integration with KMS for secret pointers.
False positives in auto-rollback could cause unnecessary disruptions; need hysteresis and human-in-the-loop overrides.
RBAC misconfiguration could allow accidental approvals — enforce least-privilege defaults and require owner review for role grants.
